book: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology, 4th ed. (Rizzo)
kicker: Lesson 14 of your course, built from Chapter 14 of your Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology textbook (Rizzo). Test practice uses checked answers, because there is no official key for this test.

steps.title: The heart and where it sits
teach: The cardiovascular system is the heart plus thousands of miles of blood vessels. The heart beats about 72 times a minute for a whole lifetime.

The heart sits obliquely between the lungs in the mediastinum, with about two-thirds of it left of the midline. It’s about the size of a closed fist: roughly 5 inches long, 3.5 inches wide and 2.5 inches thick.

options.label: In the mediastinum, between the lungs
In the pleural cavity
options.feedback: The pleural cavities hold the lungs.

steps.title: The pericardial sac
teach: The heart is enclosed in the pericardial sac (parietal pericardium), which has two layers.
The outermost layer is the fibrous pericardium: tough fibrous connective tissue that anchors the heart and stops it overstretching. The inner layer is the thin serous pericardium.
Between the serous pericardium and the heart’s surface (epicardium) is the pericardial cavity, filled with pericardial fluid to reduce friction. Inflammation here is pericarditis.

act.prompt: What is the outermost layer of the pericardial sac?

options.label: Serous pericardium
options.feedback: That’s the inner layer of the sac.

steps.title: Layers of the heart wall
teach: The epicardium (visceral pericardium) is the thin outer layer of serous tissue.
The myocardium is the second layer and makes up the bulk of the heart: involuntary, striated, branched cardiac muscle that contracts.
The endocardium is the thin inner lining of endothelium. It covers the valves and the chordae tendineae.

mnemonic.cue: Epi = on, Myo = muscle, Endo = inside
mnemonic.explanation: Epicardium is on the outside, myocardium is the muscle, endocardium lines the inside.

act.prompt: Put the heart wall layers in order, outside to inside.

steps.title: Chambers and great vessels
teach: The two upper chambers are the right and left atria; each has an ear-like auricle. The two lower chambers are the right and left ventricles. Septa separate left from right.

The right atrium receives blood from the superior vena cava (head, neck and arms), the inferior vena cava (lower body) and the coronary sinus. The right ventricle pumps it into the pulmonary trunk and pulmonary arteries to the lungs.
Four pulmonary veins bring oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left atrium. The left ventricle pumps it into the ascending aorta.
The left ventricle has the thickest walls because it pumps blood at high pressure to the whole body.

act.prompt: Which chamber receives blood from each vessel?

steps.title: Heart valves
teach: Valves keep blood from flowing backward.

Atrioventricular valves: the tricuspid valve (three cusps) is between the right atrium and right ventricle; the bicuspid, or mitral, valve (two cusps, the only two-cusp valve) is between the left atrium and left ventricle. Chordae tendineae attach the cusps to papillary muscles.
Semilunar valves: the pulmonary semilunar valve sits where the pulmonary trunk leaves the right ventricle; the aortic semilunar valve sits where the aorta leaves the left ventricle.

steps.title: Blood flow through the heart
teach: Deoxygenated blood comes in through the venae cavae to the right atrium, passes the tricuspid valve into the right ventricle, then goes through the pulmonary semilunar valve into the pulmonary arteries to the lungs.

In the lungs it drops carbon dioxide and picks up oxygen, then returns through the pulmonary veins to the left atrium, through the bicuspid valve to the left ventricle, and out through the aortic semilunar valve to the aorta.

steps.title: The conduction system
teach: The autonomic nervous system only speeds up or slows down the heart; the heart has its own conduction system that starts each beat.

The sinoatrial (SA) node in the right atrium wall is the pacemaker. It starts each cycle and sets the rate. The impulse spreads over both atria and reaches the atrioventricular (AV) node in the lower right atrium.

From the AV node, the bundle of His (atrioventricular bundle) runs down the septum and splits into right and left bundle branches, distributing the charge over the inner surfaces of the ventricles. Purkinje fibers carry it into the ventricle muscle, making the ventricles contract.

act.prompt: Put the conduction pathway in order.

steps.title: The cardiac cycle
teach: Systole is contraction; diastole is relaxation. A cardiac cycle is the systole and diastole of both atria and both ventricles.
At about 72 beats a minute, each cycle takes about 0.8 seconds: 0.1 s atria contract; 0.3 s ventricles contract; 0.4 s everything rests. So the heart muscle rests for half of every cycle.

mnemonic.explanation: Systole is contraction; diastole is relaxation.

act.prompt: How long does an average cardiac cycle take, in seconds?
act.explanation: 0.1 s atrial contraction + 0.3 s ventricular contraction + 0.4 s rest = 0.8 s.

steps.title: Circulation routes
teach: Systemic circulation: oxygenated blood leaves the left ventricle through the aorta to all body organs and returns through the venae cavae.

Coronary circulation supplies the myocardium (the coronary arteries branch off the ascending aorta). Hepatic portal circulation runs from the digestive tract to the liver; the hepatic portal vein drains the digestive organs into the liver.

Pulmonary circulation runs from the right ventricle to the lungs and back to the left atrium. Cerebral circulation supplies the brain through the carotid and vertebral arteries and the Circle of Willis. Fetal circulation is a temporary route between fetus and mother.

items.label: Right ventricle to lungs and back

steps.title: Blood vessels
teach: Arteries and veins have three layers: the tunica intima (a single layer of endothelial cells), the tunica media (smooth muscle) and the tunica adventitia (white fibrous connective tissue). The hollow core is the lumen.
Arteries are thicker, elastic and contractile. Where branches join, that’s an anastomosis. Arterioles deliver blood to capillaries.

Capillaries are microscopic vessels of simple squamous epithelium, one cell thick, where nutrients, gases and wastes are exchanged. Venules connect capillaries to veins. Veins have thinner walls and valves that keep blood moving toward the heart.

act.prompt: Put the vessels in the order blood travels from the heart and back.

steps.title: Major arteries
teach: The aorta is the largest artery: ascending aorta, aortic arch, thoracic aorta and abdominal aorta. The coronary arteries come off the ascending aorta.
From the arch: the brachiocephalic artery (right common carotid and right subclavian), the left common carotid and the left subclavian.

Thoracic branches include 10 pairs of intercostal arteries to the muscles of the thorax. Abdominal branches include the celiac trunk (stomach, spleen, liver), the superior and inferior mesenteric arteries (intestines), the renal arteries (kidneys) and the gonadal arteries. The common iliac arteries lead to the femoral, popliteal and tibial arteries of the leg.

steps.title: Major veins
teach: Veins from the head and arms drain into the superior vena cava; veins from the lower body drain into the inferior vena cava.

The median cubital vein at the elbow is usually used for drawing blood. The jugular veins drain the head. The great saphenous veins, the longest veins in the body, drain the legs. The renal veins drain the kidneys; the hepatic portal vein carries blood from the digestive organs to the liver; the hepatic veins drain the liver.

act.prompt: Which vein is usually used to draw blood?

steps.title: Heart disease
teach: Atherosclerosis: plaque builds up inside arteries, narrowing them. Coronary heart disease reduces blood flow to the myocardium and causes angina pectoris (chest pain). A myocardial infarction (heart attack) is death of heart muscle; the damaged area is an infarct.

An arrhythmia is any abnormal rhythm: bradycardia is under 60 beats a minute; tachycardia is over 100. A heart murmur is an abnormal fluttering or humming sound, often from a valve problem. Stenosis is a narrowed valve opening; an incompetent valve leaks backward.
Others: rheumatic heart disease, endocarditis, myocarditis, pericarditis, congestive heart failure, mitral valve prolapse and congenital septal defects.
Treatments include bypass surgery and angioplasty: a balloon is threaded into a coronary artery and inflated to flatten plaque, sometimes followed by a stent.

quiz.q: The outermost layer of the pericardial sac is the ______________________________.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 14 says the outermost layer of the pericardial sac is the fibrous layer, or fibrous pericardium. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 14.

quiz.q: The ______________________ circulation supplies the brain with oxygen and nutrients and disposes of waste.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 14 says the cerebral circulation supplies the brain with oxygen and nutrients and disposes of waste. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 14.

quiz.q: The _________________________ arteries supply muscles of the thorax.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 14 says there are 10 pairs of intercostal arteries that supply muscles of the thorax. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 14.

quiz.q: Any deviation from a normal heartbeat rhythm is called ______________________________.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 14 says an arrhythmia is any deviation from a normal heartbeat rhythm. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 14.

quiz.q: The mitral valve is also called the ________________________.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 14 says the valve between the left atrium and left ventricle is the bicuspid or mitral valve. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 14.

quiz.q: The reconstruction of a diseased coronary artery by inserting a small balloon through the aorta and into a coronary artery is a procedure known as __________________________________.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 14 describes angioplasty as reconstructing a diseased coronary artery by inserting a small balloon through the aorta into the artery. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 14.

quiz.q: The hollow core of a blood vessel is called the ______________________.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 14 says the hollow core of a blood vessel is the lumen. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 14.

quiz.q: An average cardiac cycle takes ________ seconds.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 14 says each cardiac cycle takes about 0.8 second. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 14.

quiz.q: Capillaries are connected to veins by ____________________________.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 14 says venules are small vessels that connect capillaries to veins. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 14.

quiz.q: The coronary arteries supply blood to the _____________________.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 14 says the coronary arteries branch off the ascending aorta and supply the heart. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 14.

quiz.q: The bundle of _________________ distributes the electrical charge over the medial surfaces of the ventricles.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 14 says the bundle of His distributes the electrical charge over the medial surfaces of the ventricles. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 14.

quiz.q: The _______________ vena cava brings blood from the upper parts of the body, the head, neck, and arms to the heart..
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 14 says the superior vena cava brings blood from the head, neck and arms. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 14.

quiz.q: The _____________________ circulation is the blood circulatory route that supplies the myocardium of the heart.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 14 says the coronary circulation route supplies the myocardium of the heart. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 14.

quiz.q: Microscopic vessels composed of simple squamous epithelial cells are called ______________________.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 14 says capillaries are microscopic vessels made of simple squamous epithelial cells. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 14.

quiz.q: The ___________________ portal vein drains the organs of the digestive tract and then continues to the liver.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 14 says the hepatic portal vein drains the organs of the digestive tract and goes to the liver. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 14.

quiz.q: The presence of ______________________ keeps blood from backflowing in the heart.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 14 says the valves prevent blood from flowing back into the pumping chamber. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 14.

quiz.q: A _______________________ is an abnormal heart sound akin to a fluttering or a humming sound.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 14 says a heart murmur is an abnormal heart sound like a fluttering or humming sound. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 14.

quiz.q: The tunica _________________________ of arteries and veins is composed of a single layer of endothelial cells.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 14 says the tunica intima is composed of a single layer of endothelial cells. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 14.

quiz.q: Oxygenated blood returns to the heart from the lungs via four pulmonary ______________________.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 14 says oxygenated blood returns to the left atrium through four pulmonary veins. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 14.

quiz.q: The second layer of the wall of the heart, the ____________________, makes up the bulk of the heart.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 14 says the myocardium, the second layer, makes up the bulk of the heart. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 14.

quiz.q: A narrowed opening through the valves of the heart is called a(n) _____________________.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 14 says stenosis of the heart valves is a narrowed opening through the valves. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 14.

quiz.q: Blood flow from the lower portions of the body return to the heart via the _______________________ vena cava.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 14 says the inferior vena cava brings blood from the lower parts of the body. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 14.

quiz.q: The right and left renal arteries supply blood to the ____________________________.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 14 says the right and left renal arteries go to the kidneys. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 14.

quiz.q: Inadequate blood flow can cause an _______________________, an area of damaged cardiac tissue.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 14 says inadequate blood flow can cause an infarct, an area of damaged cardiac tissue. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 14.

quiz.q: The heart is situated in the _______________________________, surrounded by the pericardial sac.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 14 says the heart is positioned between the lungs in the mediastinum. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 14.

quiz.q: The pulmonary semilunar valve is found in the right ventricle.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 14 places the pulmonary semilunar valve in the opening where the pulmonary trunk exits the right ventricle, so it belongs to the right ventricle. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 14.

quiz.q: The left ventricle has walls that are thicker than the right ventricle.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 14 says the left ventricle has thicker walls than the right because it pumps blood at high pressure to the whole body. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 14.

quiz.q: Systole is the term used to refer to the phase of relaxation.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Systole is contraction. Diastole is relaxation. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 14.

quiz.q: The atrioventricular node is known as the pacemaker.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. The sinoatrial (SA) node is the pacemaker, not the atrioventricular node. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 14.

quiz.q: The outermost layer of the pericardial sac is the serous pericardium.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. The outermost layer of the pericardial sac is the fibrous pericardium. The serous pericardium is the inner layer. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 14.
